articles.title: ‘Not change regime, but break country’: BJP accuses Congress of colluding with foreign powers
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) MP Nishikant Dubey on Thursday alleged that opposition-led protests in India were part of a conspiracy to
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) MP Nishikant Dubey on Thursday alleged that opposition-led protests in India were part of a conspiracy to destabilise the country.Addressing a press conference, Dubey questioned Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi’s alleged links with US lawmakers Ilhan Omar and Ro Khanna, while raising concerns over foreign funding, cryptocurrency and online gambling.Dubey alleged that foreign organisations and individuals were backing protests in an attempt to bring about a change of government in India, and claimed that Congress leaders were working in coordination with foreign elements.“All these people - whoever is in the leadership of the Congress party, whoever the opposition is - are all working together with foreign powers to not change the regime, but to break the country,” Dubey said.Questioning Rahul Gandhi’s overseas engagements, BJP MP Nishikant Dubey alleged that the Congress leader had met individuals who, according to him, were working against India’s interests.“I said in Parliament that under the guise of the Soros Foundation, he meets Ilhan Omar and Ro Khanna,” Dubey said, referring to the US lawmakers.He also questioned the Congress over Rahul’s alleged links with individuals associated with online gambling, cryptocurrency and artificial intelligence, and asked whether any of them had participated in the Congress leader’s Bharat Jodo Yatra or other journeys."My question to Congress is - Regarding Neville Roy Singham, the cartels involved in online gambling, artificial intelligence, and cryptocurrency—with which individuals from these circles has Rahul Gandhi met over the past five years? Which of these individuals have participated in his 'Bharat Jodo Yatra' or other such journeys? Moreover, whenever he travels abroad, with which of these elements does he meet, and what kind of plans do they devise to destabilise the country?" he added.Dubey also questioned whether Sam Pitroda had any role in what he described as alleged conspiracies to destabilise India. He sought details of Gandhi’s meetings during overseas visits and asked who among those he had met was associated with the Bharat Jodo Yatra.The BJP MP further referred to US congressional documents that he claimed raised concerns about foreign influence, protests and technology-related issues. He alleged that cryptocurrency, artificial intelligence and online gambling could be exploited by foreign actors to influence political movements.“The future ahead is of artificial intelligence, to destroy the entire world's economy there is cryptocurrency, and the third is online gambling,” he said, calling for greater scrutiny of these areas.Dubey also defended the government's approach to regulating online gambling and cryptocurrency, stating that online gambling had been banned and cryptocurrency did not have legal tender status in India. He said the government had taken steps to address concerns related to these activities.The BJP MP also criticised the ongoing protests in Delhi, particularly demonstrations at Jantar Mantar, alleging that they were disrupting public life.His remarks came after Delhi Police summoned Cockroach Janata Party leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka following their release from judicial custody by a Special Executive Magistrate court. Their release was subject to undertakings to maintain peace and comply with the law.The development comes as a Fox News Digital investigation titled ‘Global Chaos Inc Grows to 101 Groups’ identified 101 organisations across nine countries that it described as part of a “red-green protest ecosystem”, referring to Islamist and communist groups.The report also flagged Indian Alliance Paris (IAP), a France-based organisation, alleging that it was “connecting French and Indian protest messaging” and was “partnered with the People’s Forum in Manhattan”.It also cited an October 16 briefing by Progressive International that grouped protests in France, Spain, India and Albania, asking whether the “new rebellions can acquire the organised power to change the conditions that produced them?”. The organisation stated: “These are the forces that Progressive International is working to support and connect.”The report’s references to India come amid scrutiny of Rahul Gandhi’s overseas engagements. During his 2024 visit to the United States, the Congress leader and Lok Sabha Leader of the Opposition met several US lawmakers at the Rayburn House Office Building in Washington. The meeting was hosted by Congressman Bradley James Sherman and attended by Ilhan Omar, Ro Khanna, Raja Krishnamoorthi, Barbara Lee and others.Omar, a Democratic congresswoman from Minnesota, has drawn criticism in India over her visit to Pakistan in 2022, during which she met then-Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and former prime minister Imran Khan and travelled to Muzaffarabad in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK). India condemned the visit, describing it as “narrow-minded politics”. Reports at the time said the Pakistani government sponsored her trip and covered her accommodation and expenses.Omar was also among the US lawmakers who boycotted Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s address to a joint session of Congress.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: In 2013, former nurse Courtney Adeleye launched The Mane Choice from her kitchen with $500; within six years it had reached $100 million in sales and 60,000 retail doors before a reported $61.5 million acquisition
articles.summary: Former nurse Courtney Adeleye built a haircare business from a modest $500 investment into a brand generating more than $100 million in annual sales
articles.body: Former nurse Courtney Adeleye built a haircare business from a modest $500 investment into a brand generating more than $100 million in annual sales within six years. Her company, The Mane Choice, expanded into approximately 60,000 retail locations before its acquisition by MAV Beauty Brands in 2019 for a reported $61.5 million, according to Beauty Independent and Women’s Wear Daily. Adeleye’s journey began with a personal search for better haircare products. What started as an effort to understand and care for her natural hair eventually grew into a business that challenged established conventions in the beauty industry. Scroll down to read more…From nursing to natural haircareBased in Detroit, Adeleye trained as a nurse before turning her attention to haircare. After deciding to stop using chemical relaxers, she began documenting her natural hair journey online, sharing product recommendations, experiments and insights into hair health.Her interest in the science behind hair growth also influenced her approach. She began mixing her own formulations after finding that existing products did not meet her needs. Over time, her online audience grew, and followers began asking to purchase the products they had seen her using.In 2013, she launched The Mane Choice with $500, which covered the initial bottles, labels and ingredients. The company initially offered a deep conditioner, with Adeleye making small batches and reinvesting the proceeds into subsequent production. Rather than relying on outside investors, she expanded gradually as demand grew. The approach allowed her to retain full ownership while developing a customer base before moving into a broader product range.Supplements helped accelerate growthAlthough the company began with haircare, its expansion into supplements proved pivotal. Adeleye introduced products designed to complement haircare routines, tapping into growing consumer interest in hair health and nutrition. A promotional campaign on Black Friday generated more than $30,000 in orders after a discount-code error led to unexpectedly high demand. The surge created a fulfilment challenge because the company had only 500 supplement units available.Adeleye contacted customers to explain the situation and offered refunds or free shipping once additional stock arrived. The response helped demonstrate the loyalty her brand had developed among early buyers. Supplements subsequently became a major driver of the company’s growth. The Mane Choice also secured retail distribution through major chains, including Walmart and Target, bringing its products to a substantially wider audience.A $61.5 million acquisitionBy the time The Mane Choice reached its sixth year, the company was generating more than $100 million in annual sales. Adeleye began exploring its valuation, initially seeking to understand the financial strength of the business rather than necessarily planning an immediate sale. In 2019, she agreed to sell the company to MAV Beauty Brands in a deal reported at $61.5 million. Her complete ownership of the business meant she could make the decision without negotiating with outside equity investors.The sale also marked a turning point in her approach to brand building. The Mane Choice's identity was closely tied to haircare, which Adeleye later recognised could make expansion into skincare and body care more complicated.Building again with Watch & Sea BeautyAdeleye did not step away from entrepreneurship permanently. In 2022, she launched Olbali, a beauty and wellness platform that included several brands. She later closed the venture to concentrate on Watch & Sea Beauty, a business spanning haircare, skincare and body care.The new brand officially launched in December 2024, followed by the introduction of its Flourishing Collection in early 2025. The haircare range entered 200 Target stores in February that year, building on relationships Adeleye had established with retailers during her earlier venture, according to Beauty Independent and theGrio. Watch & Sea also reflects lessons learned from her first company. Adeleye has emphasised the importance of developing products around consumer needs, investing in research and building a business with room to expand beyond a single category.Her journey illustrates how a small, self-funded venture can grow through customer trust, product development and strategic retail partnerships. From mixing haircare products at home to negotiating a multimillion-dollar acquisition and returning to the industry with a new brand, Adeleye has built her career around identifying gaps in the market and finding ways to address them. The next chapter is no longer about proving she can build a successful haircare company. It is about applying those lessons to a broader beauty business while preserving the consumer relationships that helped her first venture grow.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.body: Patna: A worker died and 12 others were injured after a truck carrying them to Hajipur overturned on Bakhtiyarpur-Patna four-lane near Madhopur village in Patna district on Thursday morning.The deceased was identified as Mallik Rai, a resident of Mekra village under Mokama police station area. articles.title: 80% of India’s insurance buying journey now happens online, Google-McKinsey report claims
articles.summary: Insurance buying in India is increasingly shifting towards online.
articles.body: Insurance buying in India is increasingly shifting towards online. According to a new study by Google, with McKinsey & Company as its knowledge partner, nearly 80% of India's insurance buying journey now happens online, with consumers using search engines and videos to research policies before approaching an advisor. The report also found that digital research directly influences 40% of health and life insurance sales.‘Decoding the DICA Consumer’ study shows an expanding category of purchasers who shop for insurance providers and filter options online before turning to human assistance to complete the purchase. The findings indicate that digital platforms are influencing insurance decisions, but customers still value a human adviser's input on policy wording, cover, and future financial security.Why Indians are buying insurance onlineThe report identifies these consumers as Digitally Influenced, Closed with Assistance (DICA) buyers. They research policies online, shortlist insurers and then approach advisors to validate their choices and understand policy details.Siddharth Shekar, Director, Google India, said, “The DICA consumer highlights that purchasing insurance in India is an intricate journey where no single touchpoint or advisor operates in isolation. When the digital ecosystem directly influences more than 40% of all insurance purchases the online shortlist becomes an important decisive factor. Closing the gap between a consumer's digital evaluation and their offline advisory experience is now the biggest lever for insurance penetration and value creation.”The report found that 78% of consumers narrow their choices to two or three insurance brands online before speaking to an advisor. More than 50% of consumers continue to prefer their original online shortlist even after consulting an agent.The findings indicate that advisors increasingly need to answer specific questions about coverage, policy exclusions, and service support rather than introduce buyers to insurance brands from scratch.Non-metro consumers and salaried professionals lead online researchOnline insurance research is not limited to consumers in metropolitan cities. According to the study, consumers in leading non-metro cities conduct roughly twice as much online research before purchasing a policy compared with the national average.Salaried professionals aged 25–35 represent the largest demographic driving this digital research. The group also shows higher engagement with comparison tools and policy explainers across age groups.The report calls on insurers to involve consumers at the research stage when they're considering options, rather than only through traditional sales channels.AI search and YouTube influence insurance decisionsAI-powered search tools and video content are helping consumers understand insurance products. The study found that longer queries account for 18% of insurance searches on Google, reflecting demand for information about specific coverage requirements and complicated policy terms.It also found that 41% of users use AI Overviews to compare options and establish their coverage requirements before approaching an insurer.Video is another important part of the buying journey. Approximately 60% of online insurance researchers use videos during their research, while insurance-related content on YouTube crossed 2.5 billion views in India over the past year. More than 15% of these views occurred on YouTube Connected TV, suggesting insurance research can also involve discussions among household members.Meanwhile, insurance mobile apps are seeing increased engagement for routine activities such as tracking policies and managing claims.Why insurance buyers still need human assistanceDespite the shift towards online research, the study found that fewer than 30% of buyers are comfortable purchasing high-value insurance policies entirely through digital checkout processes.Consumers still seek help understanding policy exclusions, confirming long-term financial security, and getting support during hospital claims. However, the transition from online research to offline sales is not always seamless.More than 40% of buyers said they were frustrated by having to repeat their requirements after being contacted as new leads. More than a third also cited generic sales scripts that did not reflect their specific needs.The report found that offline insurance purchases influenced by online research generate policy premiums approximately 40% higher than traditional sales.Parthanil Ghosh, Managing Director and CEO, HDFC ERGO General Insurance, said, “The emergence of the DICA consumers will boost awareness and accessibility in the insurance sector. For insurers, enabling this journey seamlessly across their omnichannel distribution network, like advisors, websites, mobile apps and other digital platforms, can help in building consumer confidence and trust, and thereby increase insurance penetration in India.”Sumit Madan, Managing Director and CEO, Axis Max Life Insurance, said, “The future of insurance distribution will not be defined by where customers buy, but by how effectively we connect digital discovery with trusted advice. When more than 40% of policies are already digitally influenced, the industry's next growth opportunity lies in converting informed intent into meaningful protection.”The study's findings are based on a survey of 1,039 insurance consumers; aggregated, masked lead-to-conversion analysis across life and health insurers; interviews with industry advisors and distribution platforms; and insights from Google and McKinsey.You use AI every day. articles.summary: The much-awaited trailer of Keerthy Suresh and Radhika Apte starrer 'Akka' is finally out, offering a glimpse into the rivalry between two \"female
articles.body: The much-awaited trailer of Keerthy Suresh and Radhika Apte starrer 'Akka' is finally out, offering a glimpse into the rivalry between two "female gangsters" to protect their reign.Produced by YRF Entertainment and directed by Dharmaraj Shetty, the trailer takes viewers into the kingdom of Pernuru and its powerful houses. It teases a world where women lead from the front and fiercely guard what is theirs.Keerthy Suresh, portraying the role of an impeccable leader and fighter, faces the challenge from Radhika Apte who wishes to challenge the legacy that has long ruled Pernuru. The trailer is full of action scenes and impactful dialogues."At the heart of Akka are Bhavani (Keerthy Suresh) and Rudra (Radhika Apte) — two formidable women whose differing ambitions and beliefs fuel a gripping rivalry. As their conflict threatens to disrupt the established order, the series explores themes of power, loyalty, family, and revenge," read the press note shared by Netflix.Led by Keerthy Suresh and Radhika Apte, the ensemble also features Tanvi Azmi, Mahesh Manjrekar, Anshuman Pushkar, and Monica Panwar, amongst others.Netflix shared the trailer on their Instagram handle on Thursday.Reflecting on stepping into the role of Bhavani, Keerthy Suresh said, “Bhavani is a woman who knows what she stands for and will go to great lengths to protect her legacy. What makes her interesting is that beneath her strength and authority are choices that are never easy, especially when the stakes are so high. The trailer offers a taste of the world she inhabits and the challenges that come her way. Working with Radhika was amazing because Bhavani and Rudra bring such different energies to the story, and their dynamic adds another layer of tension to the narrative. It's been wonderful partnering with YRF Entertainment to bring this story to life and with Netflix to take Akka to audiences across India and beyond. I hope audiences enjoy discovering the many sides of Bhavani as the story unfolds,” as quoted in a press note.Speaking about Rudra and her experience on the series, Radhika Apte said, “Rudra is someone who refuses to be defined by the circumstances she finds herself in. She is fierce, has her own ambitions, and is willing to challenge the established order, which makes her a fascinating character to explore. What I enjoyed about Akka is that the conflict isn't simply about who holds power; it's also about the different beliefs, loyalties, and personal stakes that drive each character. It was exciting to see these contrasting worldviews come to life through Rudra and Bhavani, and an absolute joy to share the screen with Keerthy in bringing their intense face-off to life. I'm glad to have been part of this collaboration between Netflix and YRF Entertainment, and I look forward to audiences experiencing the intensity of this powerful story.”'Akka' is set to premiere on October 30 on Netflix.

articles.summary: Two neighbours in Michigan, United States, spent years fighting over water flowing between their properties, with each accusing the other of causing
articles.body: Two neighbours in Michigan, United States, spent years fighting over water flowing between their properties, with each accusing the other of causing flooding and damage. Their dispute eventually reached court, where a jury awarded $85,000 to William Michael Coan and Cindy Plant and $91,250 to their neighbour, Robert Ercolani. Both sides challenged parts of the earlier court decisions, but on Tuesday, the Michigan Court of Appeals upheld the rulings, including the compensation awards and a plan to improve drainage between their properties.The disagreement unfolded along North Latson Road in Livingston County. Coan owned a property at number 800 and shared ownership of another property at number 790 with his girlfriend, Plant. Ercolani owned number 796, located between the two. The flooding mainly affected the properties at numbers 800 and 796.According to the judgment, the properties had largely been free from flooding before Coan and Plant acquired their land. However, the neighbours disagreed about what caused the problem to begin. Over time, both Coan and Ercolani changed parts of their properties, including raising or lowering sections of the ground. These changes became important because even alterations to ground levels can affect where rainwater collects and how it moves.What might have been a disagreement over drainage turned into years of court proceedings where both sides accused the other of allowing water to enter their land.Beginning of the disputeA major part of the disagreement concerned changes made to Coan's property. Ercolani maintained that his land had not flooded before work began on the neighbouring plot.He alleged that changes to the ground had caused water to flow towards his property. There were also accusations that water had been pumped across the boundary.During the proceedings, an engineer examined soil samples, aerial photographs and maps showing the ground levels. The evidence indicated that additional soil had been placed on Coan's land, changing the way surface water moved.The engineer found that some water which had previously collected on Coan's property was instead being directed towards Ercolani's land.Witnesses also described seeing Coan pump water towards the neighbouring property. Ercolani said he had built a raised earth barrier to protect his land because he was tired of the flooding.But Coan and Plant had complaints of their own. They accused Ercolani of causing water to enter their property and sought compensation for the damage. With both sides blaming each other, the dispute eventually reached a jury.Both neighbours receive compensationWhen the jury considered the evidence, it did not hold only one side responsible. On one hand, it found that Ercolani had caused damage to Coan and Plant's property through water entering their land. They were awarded $85,000 for damage to property other than trees.On the other hand, the jury also found that Coan had caused damage to Ercolani's property. Ercolani was awarded $91,250.Plant was found to have allowed water to enter Ercolani's property unlawfully, but the jury concluded that her actions had not caused damage.The jury also examined whether either side had acted negligently. It found that Coan and Plant had not been negligent. Ercolani was found negligent, but the jury decided that his negligence had not directly caused the damage claimed against him.The result was that both sides received substantial compensation, although neither succeeded on every claim. Yet the money did not solve the problem that had brought them to court. Water still needed a route across the properties, and the neighbours could not agree on how to manage it.New drainage plan to address floodingBoth sides suggested their own ways of dealing with the water. The judge, however, was not satisfied with either proposal. Instead, the court asked an independent expert, Wayne Perry, to examine the situation and recommend a solution.Perry proposed several measures, including areas where water and sediment could collect, changes to the slope of the land and underground pipes to carry water between the properties. His proposal also included a French drain, an underground drainage system that allows water to move through a channel beneath the ground.The judge concluded that the land had changed so much over the years that returning it to its earlier condition was no longer practical.There was another difficulty. The neighbours had been involved in a long and bitter dispute, making a solution that depended on their cooperation difficult to manage.The court therefore wanted a drainage arrangement that could work with minimal involvement from either side. It selected Perry's proposal, finding it more suitable than the alternatives.Neither side was satisfied with every aspect of the decision, and the drainage plan became another issue in their appeals.Appeals court upholds earlier decisionsThe neighbours challenged several parts of the trial court's rulings, including the handling of expert evidence and the choice of drainage plan.Ercolani also disputed an earlier finding that he had violated a court order restricting him from pumping water onto neighbouring land. For that violation, he had been fined $2,900. After legal fees were added, the amount reached $8,147.50. The appeals court rejected his challenge to that decision.
